newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Minfins edge up, wait for US CPI.
newsitem.headline: Russian Minfins edge up, wait for US CPI.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged up in thin trading on Thursday following a rise in U.S. Treasuries, and dealers said the market was waiting for the U.S. July consumer price index to be released at 1230 GMT.
Dealers said they expected only a modest rise in CPI after Wednesday's unexpected fall in July producer prices, but were mixed on how far this would push up MinFin bond prices.
"Everthing is a bit stronger as the paper is tracking U.S. Treasuries," a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said.
The 30-year U.S. bonds rose after the U.S. July producer price index slipped by 0.1 percent against the market expectations that it would rise.
The Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said MinFins could be much stronger, if CPI was good.
"I cannot see why it should not rise," she said.
Market fears of a big rise in CPI, pointing to rising inflation pressures, have abated and dealers said they expected CPI to be favourable for the market.
"Today's figure will make the situation completely clear," an Aljba-Alliance dealer said. "Most people think it will not be worse than expected."
But he forecast only a slight rise after the figure came out, if no other good news from Russia came.
According to a Reuters poll, economists forecast the year-on-year rise in the CPI at 2.4 percent after 2.3 percent in June.
